title: Short seeds for autokey ciphers
reader_title: Can earlier runes extend a short starting key?
reader_intro: Tries named words and two- or three-rune starting keys that grow using earlier encrypted or recovered runes, plus a separate four-rune key spelling DEOR, not the text of the Old English poem.

reader_test.input: Archived rune text on LP2-04 through LP2-37, with three-rune starting keys tested on 31 eligible pages and the distinct four-rune DEOR key on LP2-04 through LP2-13.
reader_test.action: Try named words and every two- or three-rune starting key, plus one four-rune DEOR key, extending each key with earlier recovered or encrypted runes and restarting it on each page.
reader_test.check: Except for four-rune DEOR, single-rune words must become I or A before the whole-page rune-frequency test; a candidate must pass that fixed frequency threshold.

question: Do the pinned source keyword, two-rune, or three-rune autokey seeds pass their one-rune and IoC screens on the selected LP2 pages?
reader_question: Could a short word or rune seed drive an autokey cipher?
summary: Four related archived search branches were replayed on verified LP2 page streams. None passed the source-defined hit screen; the gate and ciphertext-feedback design sharply limit what that result can exclude.
finding: Across the four source branches, zero manuscript outputs passed their strict IoC > 1.3 hit threshold. The 4,488 named-keyword settings had 135 one-rune-compatible cases; 171,564 two-rune settings had 5,058; 4,536,354 three-rune settings had none on 31 source-eligible pages. The distinct four-rune DEOR vector gave zero hits among 60 IoC-only settings. A planted reading-like control passed in all six feedback modes.
limitations: The source requires visible one-rune words to decode to I or A, which assumes this word segmentation and language. Ciphertext-feedback seeds alter only their own short output prefix, so the whole-page screen cannot reliably identify those seeds. Forty-nine full-search shuffles are coarse controls, not a cipher model. Other seed lengths, pages, boundaries and autokey rules remain untested.
next_steps: Predeclare a seed-specific prediction of a longer passage or independently measurable feature, then check it on held-out pages without selecting another favorable key afterward.

scope.representation: Pinned archived source GP29 page values verified against current LP2-04–37 text; source pages old21–54 map to LP2-(old−17). Source isolated-word positions retained.
scope.procedure: Replay six GP29 plaintext/ciphertext feedback recurrences for 22 source keyword seeds, every two-rune seed, every three-rune seed on source-eligible pages, and the one distinct four-rune P21–30 DEOR array. Preserve source gates, strict IoC threshold and page resets; compare 49 full-search shuffles.
scope.parameters: 4,488 named-keyword, 171,564 two-rune, 4,536,354 three-rune, and 60 distinct P21–30 DEOR settings; 49 within-page shuffled complete searches, seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Other seeds or lengths, alternate alphabets, word resets and segmentations, different singleton assumptions, English scoring, the P21–30 running-key/double-layer branches, and manuscript-derived numerical autokey rules without an exact recurrence.

review.kind: pinned archived-source replay with sampled original-function parity and full-search shuffle controls
review.reviewer: Original-function parity on sampled decodes and full small grids; independent scalar reconstruction of every saved winner, input hash, and control comparison.

reproduction.environment: Python 3 with NumPy and Numba. Optional source_parity.py and gate_check.py require a local checkout of the pinned upstream commit; the replay uses bundled verified inputs.

visuals.caption: One row per source-defined branch: searched settings, one-rune-compatible settings and hits. The P21–30 variant has no one-rune gate.

browser_followups.title: DIVINITY plaintext autokey: restart each word
browser_followups.question: Does DIVINITY-seeded plaintext autokey, restarted at each transcription word, recover the fixed 24-rune Warning opening on the four declared pages?
browser_followups.scope_change: Change the source DIVINITY autokey from page resets to a newly specified reset at every non-rune character. Limit the check to LP2-16, LP2-27, LP2-32 and LP2-35, whose first 24 runes enter feedback within a word longer than the eight-index seed. This differs from FH3, which repeats a key after its seed rather than feeding back plaintext or ciphertext.
browser_followups.limitation: A match concerns only this 24-rune opening, not a complete reading or other seeds. On LP2-32 and LP2-35 the first 12 outputs are equivalent to repeating-key word reset; the feedback distinction enters later. FH3 used English scores rather than a failed exact Warning-prefix criterion. Headings remain included; no interruptions, phase search or cross-word history is allowed.

value.detail: Test only the fixed 24-rune Warning opening under the declared hypothesis; a match is not a complete decipherment.

control.label: Recover the known Warning text from synthetic ciphertext
